With 3 days on Koh Samui, arrive and eat at Fisherman's Village, spend one day on a boat (Ang Thong from 16 December to 31 October, Pig Island on any date) and drive the round-island sights loop. Five days adds the Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat trip and a west-coast sunset; 7 days adds Koh Phangan and a slow wellness day; 10 days adds a night in Ang Thong Marine Park.

Good to know: Ang Thong Marine Park is closed every year from 1 November to 15 December. Season reopens 16 December. Book now for later dates. In that window, follow the November version below and swap Ang Thong for the Pig Island speedboat tour (1,450 THB) or the Koh Tao day trip (2,200 THB).

One day on Koh Samui

On a stopover or a cruise-ship call, keep it simple and stay in the north-east, near the airport and piers.

  1. 08:00 Big Buddha and Wat Plai Laem before the heat (both free).
  2. 10:00 Swim and lunch at Choeng Mon or North Chaweng.
  3. 14:00 Lad Koh viewpoint and Hin Ta and Hin Yai at the south end of Lamai.
  4. 16:30 Fisherman's Village for a massage (about 300–600 THB an hour), shops and an early dinner.

If you would rather spend the day on the water, the Pig Island speedboat tour (4–5 hours) fits a single day with time to spare.

3 days on Koh Samui

Three full days is enough for the essentials if you base yourself in Chaweng, Bophut or Choeng Mon, close to the airport and to most tour pickups.

Day 1: arrive, Chaweng or Fisherman's Village

  1. Afternoon Land at Samui Airport; taxi to the main resort areas about 400–700 THB depending on zone, or Grab from just outside the pickup lane.
  2. 16:00 Swim at North Chaweng or Choeng Mon while the sun is lower.
  3. 18:00 Sunset drink at Fisherman's Village, Bophut (the sun sets around 17:55–18:45 depending on the month).
  4. 19:00 Dinner in Fisherman's Village. On a Friday the walking street runs about 17:00–23:00; on Monday and Wednesday there are smaller markets. On Thursday to Saturday, Chaweng Walking Street by Chaweng Lake is the alternative.

Day 2: Ang Thong Marine Park, or Pig Island from 1 November to 15 December

  1. 07:30–08:30 Hotel pickup for the Ang Thong speedboat tour (1,800 THB adult, 1,400 THB child; park fee 300/150 THB cash).
  2. Morning Snorkelling, then the viewpoint on Koh Wua Talap (a steep staircase of about 20–30 minutes) and kayaking.
  3. Midday Lunch, then the Emerald Lake (Thale Nai) on Koh Mae Ko.
  4. 16:30–17:00 Back at your hotel.

From 1 November to 15 December, take the Pig Island and Koh Tan speedboat tour instead: 4–5 hours from Thong Krut, 1,450 THB adult and 1,250 THB child, with about 50 THB cash for Koh Madsum where not included.

Day 3: the round-island loop

The ring road is about 51 km. With stops, the classic loop takes a full day by car, taxi (about 2,000–3,000 THB for the day) or scooter.

  1. 08:30 Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai), on its causeway near Bang Rak; free, 07:00–18:30. Go early before the heat and coach groups.
  2. 09:15 Wat Plai Laem, about 1 km east: the 18-armed Guanyin on the lake; free.
  3. 10:15 Lad Koh viewpoint on the ring road between Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove; stay off the wet rocks.
  4. 11:00 Hin Ta and Hin Yai at the south end of Lamai; free, parking about 30 THB.
  5. 12:00 Lunch in Lamai.
  6. 13:30 Wat Khunaram on Route 4169, home of the mummified monk Luang Pho Daeng; cover shoulders and knees.
  7. 14:15 Na Muang Waterfall 1 (free, 09:00–17:00; parking 20 THB scooter, 60 THB car); swim in the pool.
  8. 17:30 Sunset on the west coast at Nathon pier or Lipa Noi.

Want more temples? See Koh Samui temples and waterfalls.

5 days on Koh Samui

Days 1–3 as above

Follow the 3-day plan, ideally with your boat day early in the trip so you can move it if the sea is rough.

Day 4: Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan

The Koh Tao and Koh Nang Yuan speedboat trip takes about 8–9 hours door to door and costs 2,200 THB adult and 1,600 THB child. You snorkel in Koh Tao's bays and climb the viewpoint above the Nang Yuan sandbar. Bring 250 THB cash for the Nang Yuan landing fee; plastic bottles are not allowed on the island.

Day 5: Pig Island sunset tour or a west-coast beach day

Spend the morning on the beach, then take the Pig Island sunset tour (1,550 THB adult, about 5–6 hours with dinner). If you have already been to Pig Island, drive to the west coast: Lipa Noi for a shallow, calm swim at high tide, then Taling Ngam for sunset over the Five Islands.

7 days on Koh Samui

Days 1–5 as above, then:

Day 6: Koh Phangan, or a Full Moon night if your dates align

Koh Phangan is 20–50 minutes away by boat. For a day trip, take a scheduled boat from the Bangrak piers or Maenam to Thong Sala and hire a driver on Phangan, or charter a private speedboat to Koh Phangan and choose your beaches. If your week includes a Full Moon Party (24 November, 24 December and 31 December 2026; 22 January and 22 February 2027), our Full Moon Party speedboat costs 1,400 THB return with hotel pickup and drop-off on Samui. Party entry (about 200 THB) is paid at the gate.

Day 7: cooking class, ethical elephant sanctuary or spa

Slow down. Take a Thai cooking class, visit an ethical elephant sanctuary (choose a no-riding, no-bathing venue; half days cost about 3,000 THB), or book a spa afternoon. A one-hour Thai massage costs about 300–500 THB at a local shop.

A 10-day itinerary

Days 1–7 as above, then:

Days 8–9: Ang Thong overnight

Stay a night inside Ang Thong Marine Park, on Koh Wua Talap, after the day boats leave. Choose the tent overnight (3,600 THB adult, 3,400 THB child) or the bungalow overnight (4,200 THB adult, 3,900 THB child). You get the viewpoint at sunrise, kayaking in quiet water and a sky full of stars. The park fee (300/150 THB cash) is extra. Both run from 16 December to 31 October. If you already did the Ang Thong day trip on Day 2, use these two days for the Pink Dolphins and Pig Island tour (2,250 THB) and a beach day.

Day 10: market, massage, goodbye

Morning at the Hua Thanon fish market or Lamai fresh market (06:00–20:00), a last massage, then the airport. Leave at least 90 minutes before a domestic flight and more on Friday afternoons in Chaweng traffic.

A second loop: the quiet south and west

With 7 days or more, add a second land day that covers the south and west coasts, which most visitors never see. It suits a car or a driver, because the south-west connector (Route 4170) is steep and winding.

  1. 08:30 Hua Thanon fish market and Muslim fishing village on the south-east coast; mornings are best.
  2. 09:30 Guan Yu Shrine on the hillside near Hua Thanon, with its 16 m bronze statue; free, 09:00–17:00.
  3. 10:15 Wat Ratchathammaram (Wat Sila Ngu, the "Red Temple") between Lamai and Hua Thanon, covered in carved terracotta reliefs; allow 30 minutes.
  4. 11:15 Laem Sor Pagoda at the end of Bang Kao beach, a gold-tiled chedi on the shore; free, 07:00–18:00.
  5. 12:30 Seafood lunch in Taling Ngam; Baan Suan Lung Khai, a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand for 2026, needs a reservation.
  6. 14:30 Nathon old town: the waterfront, old shophouses and the pier.
  7. 16:00 Swim at Lipa Noi at high tide.
  8. 17:45 Sunset at Taling Ngam or Nathon pier.

Combine it with a Pig Island afternoon from Thong Krut if you start early. Details of each stop are on the places map.

A two-week version: Samui, Phangan and Tao

For 14 days in the Gulf, split the trip and move by scheduled ferry between islands:

  • Days 1–7 on Samui: the 7-day plan above, with Ang Thong (or Pig Island in November) and the round-island loop.
  • Days 8–10 on Koh Phangan: ferry from Samui (20–50 minutes, about 200–500 THB). Beaches in the north, yoga and, if the dates match, the Full Moon Party on your doorstep.
  • Days 11–13 on Koh Tao: ferry from Phangan, about 1–1.5 hours. Snorkel or dive, with a Discover Scuba or a few fun dives.
  • Day 14: fast boat back to Samui (1 h 30–2 h, about 700 THB) for your flight. Allow a margin: in the monsoon, take the morning boat and fly the next day.

Our tour boats return to Samui each evening, so use them for day trips while you are based on Samui and the scheduled ferries to move between islands.

The November to mid-December version

From 1 November to 15 December, Ang Thong is closed and November is the wettest month (about 445 mm over 16 rain days). Keep the shape of the plan but make these swaps:

Normal planNovember–15 December swap
Ang Thong day tourPig Island and Koh Tan speedboat (1,450 THB), all year
Ang Thong overnightPink Dolphins and Pig Island (2,250 THB) or a private longtail to Pig Island (5,950 THB per boat)
Koh Tao day tripKeep it, but book it early in your stay so it can move if the sea is rough
Beach afternoon in Chaweng or LamaiHotel pool, or a sheltered bay such as Choeng Mon; never swim on red-flag days
Outdoor market nightCentral Samui mall, Muay Thai night (no fights on Thursdays) or a cooking class

Rainy-day backups are listed further down. On 24 November 2026 the Full Moon Party and Loy Krathong fall on the same night; on Samui, float a krathong at Chaweng Lake or Big Buddha (sky lanterns are banned). More in Koh Samui in November.

Itineraries by travel style

Couples and honeymoon

Stay in Bophut, Choeng Mon or a west-coast villa. Add the Ang Thong VIP tour (4,500 THB, only 15 guests on a big speedboat) the private Pig Island speedboat (11,950 THB per boat, up to 10 guests) or the private Ang Thong speedboat (33,000 THB per boat), a sunset dinner in Taling Ngam and a spa day. See Koh Samui honeymoon.

Families with children

Base in Choeng Mon or Lipa Noi. Pig Island (4–5 hours, children 1,250 THB) is the best first boat trip: short crossing, pigs on the beach, easy snorkelling at Koh Tan. Children's life jackets are provided and must be worn. Infants aged 0–2 travel free. For Ang Thong, the big boat tour (1,500 THB adult, 1,100 THB child, about 10 hours) is a cheaper, steadier alternative to the speedboat for families. See Koh Samui with kids.

Party trips

Stay in Central Chaweng. Plan around a Full Moon Party (shared speedboat 1,400 THB) or a Half Moon Festival Magic Forest night (packages from 2,700 THB; 2–3 and 16–17 December 2026). Add ARKbar and Soi Green Mango on other nights. See nightlife and party calendar.

Wellness

Mornings of yoga, afternoons in a spa or jungle rock pools, early nights. Base in Lamai's hills, Choeng Mon or the south-east. Keep one boat day for Pig Island. See retreats and yoga.

Divers and snorkellers

Come between February and October (clearest water March–April). Do Ang Thong, Koh Tao and Nang Yuan, and a Sail Rock dive day. See diving and snorkelling.

Where to stay for each itinerary

  • 3 days: Chaweng, Bophut or Choeng Mon, 5–15 minutes from the airport and in the main pickup zone.
  • 5–7 days: the same, or Lamai for value. Bophut and Maenam are handy for Koh Phangan boats.
  • 10 days or more: split the stay, for example 5 nights in Chaweng or Bophut and 4 on the west coast for sunsets and quiet.
  • With Pig Island trips: anywhere; hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui. Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut (and other remote areas) add 400 THB per person, return, on most tours.

Booking ahead

  • Online cut-off: booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thailand time (ICT). For same-day requests, message us on WhatsApp.
  • Confirmation: after payment we confirm your booking by email or WhatsApp and send your pickup time the evening before.
  • Full Moon nights and the Half Moon Festival sell out first; book several days ahead.
  • 20 December–5 January is the busiest fortnight of the year for boats, hotels and flights. Book boat days as soon as your flights are fixed.

  • Ages: adults 12+, children 3–11 pay the child price, and infants aged 0–2 travel free.

Getting around on an itinerary

  • Boat days: our tours include hotel pickup from most areas of the island, so you need no transport on those days.
  • Grab: works best in Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai; short hops about 80–120 THB, cross-island 200–350 THB.
  • Full-day taxi: about 2,000–3,000 THB for the round-island loop, the easiest way to do Day 3 without riding.
  • Songthaews: 30–80 THB along the ring road by day, cash only, scarce after 20:00.
  • Scooter: 150–350 THB a day. You need an International Driving Permit with the motorcycle category, and a helmet (fines up to 2,000 THB). See scooter rental.

More in getting around Koh Samui.

Mistakes to avoid

  • Khao Sok as a day trip: it is 4–6 hours each way from Samui. Do it as 2 days and 1 night or not at all.
  • Ang Thong in November: the park is closed from 1 November to 15 December. Book Pig Island instead.
  • A boat day on your flight day: weather delays happen. Keep the last day on land.
  • Swimming at Bophut: it is a dining beach, not a swimming beach. Go to Choeng Mon or Chaweng.
  • Ignoring red flags: rip currents on Chaweng and Lamai have drowned swimmers who ignored red flags, especially from October to December.
  • Riding without an IDP: your travel insurance will usually refuse a scooter claim without a licence that covers motorcycles.
  • Planning one-way island hops on tour boats: tour boats return to the island they left from.

Rainy-day ideas

  • Central Samui mall in Chaweng: shops, restaurants and a food court.
  • Thai cooking class: half-day classes run morning or evening; see cooking classes.
  • Spa or massage: 300–500 THB for an hour of Thai massage; resort spas from about 1,800 THB.
  • Muay Thai: fights every night except Thursday, under cover.
  • Temples: Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem and Wat Khunaram are quick visits between showers.
  • Waterfalls after rain: Na Muang 1 is spectacular after a downpour, but stay out of the water when it is brown and fast.

Adding nearby islands

  • Koh Phangan: 20–50 minutes by boat; stay 2–3 nights for its beaches, yoga and the Full Moon Party, or visit in a day. See Koh Phangan.
  • Koh Tao: 1 h 30–2 h by fast boat; stay 2–3 nights to dive, or visit in a day with our speedboat tour. See Koh Tao.
  • Khao Sok: 2 days and 1 night minimum via the Donsak ferry and about 190 km of road.

Our tour boats always return to the island they left from; there is no one-way island hopping on tour boats. To move on to Phangan or Tao, use the scheduled ferries (see Koh Samui to Koh Phangan and Koh Samui to Koh Tao) or a private transfer. Compare the three islands in Samui vs Phangan vs Tao.

Markets and night food by day

  • Every day: Lamai Night Market (by the river bridge, from about 17:00), Si Khao Night Market off Chaweng Beach Road (17:00–23:00), Central Samui market, Nathon night food market (16:30–22:00).
  • Monday and Wednesday: smaller markets at Fisherman's Village.
  • Tuesday: Nathon night market at its busiest.
  • Thursday to Saturday: Chaweng Walking Street beside Chaweng Lake.
  • Friday: Fisherman's Village Walking Street, about 17:00–23:00. Arrive by 17:30–18:00 and park at The Wharf.
  • Mornings: Hua Thanon fish market and Lamai fresh market.

Street prices: pad thai 60–80 THB, mango sticky rice 50–80 THB, grilled prawns 80–120 THB. See Koh Samui markets.

Itineraries with a toddler or grandparents

Choose low-walking options and short transfers:

  • Boat trips: Pig Island is the gentlest, with a short crossing and flat beaches. On Ang Thong, the big boat is steadier than a speedboat in a swell.
  • Ang Thong viewpoint warning: the climb on Koh Wua Talap is a steep staircase of about 20–30 minutes with uneven steps. Many older visitors and small children skip it and stay on the beach or kayak instead.
  • Easy sights: Big Buddha, Wat Plai Laem and Hin Ta and Hin Yai are a few minutes from the car park. Na Muang 1 is a short, flat walk; Na Muang 2 is a steep climb.
  • Base: Choeng Mon or North Chaweng, 5–15 minutes from the airport and a hospital.
  • Midday: plan indoor time from 12:00 to 15:00, when the heat is strongest.

How we plan an itinerary for guests

Our Australian-Thai team has run boat trips around Samui since 2006. Send us your dates, where you are staying and what you enjoy on WhatsApp, and we will suggest which boat day fits which date, check the sea forecast, and flag clashes such as a Full Moon night or a closure. We only recommend trips we run or know well, and we will tell you honestly when a trip is not worth it in the weather.

Before you go: final checks

  • TDAC: file the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card at tdac.immigration.go.th within 3 days before arrival.
  • Visa: most nationalities get 30 days visa-free since 15 September 2026. See the Thailand visa guide.
  • Driving: bring an International Driving Permit with the motorcycle category if you plan to ride.
  • Cash for island fees: Ang Thong 300 THB (child 150), Koh Nang Yuan 250 THB, Koh Madsum about 50 THB.
  • Insurance: make sure it covers boat trips and scooters. See travel insurance.
  • Boat-day kit: seasickness tablets, reef-safe sunscreen, a rash vest, water shoes and a dry bag for your phone; leave passports in the hotel safe.
  • Weather: check the forecast and sea state the day before each boat day on sea conditions.
